target: workflow.sh merge — running merge twice against the same template leaves the second run's bytes identical to the first run's result (a re-run is a silent no-op)
cmd: source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/workflow.sh"; source "$FIXTURES/workflow-fixture.sh"; wf_file project.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("old");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// bottom'; wf_file template.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("new");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// bottom'; FIRST=$(workflow_merge project.js template.js '//' '{}'); cp project.js after_first.js; SECOND=$(workflow_merge project.js template.js '//' '{}'); MATCH=$(cmp -s project.js after_first.js && echo true || echo false); jq -n --argjson f "$FIRST" --argjson s "$SECOND" --argjson match "$MATCH" '{first:$f, second:$s, match:$match}'
_note: Guards the cmp-before-write guard in workflow_merge: once a region matches the template, a re-run must classify it unchanged (not refreshed again) and must not rewrite the file — verified with a byte-exact cmp between the post-first-merge and post-second-merge file, not just 'no error'.
